text:
🔴|3 November 2026: The Ledger Across Six Fronts. The Refueling Package Is in the Air. The Giants Brigades Lost a General. The Corridor Is Being Defended by India.

🇾🇪 Yemen: The Factory in Al-Taiziyah

Saudi fighter jets struck a factory in Al-Taiziyah district, Taiz governorate. At least three killed, eight injured. Al-Masirah reports the figures are preliminary.

Al-Taiziyah sits at 13.58°N 44.02°E, immediately north of Taiz city on the road to Ibb. It is a civilian district markets, workshops, light industry, residential blocks. A "factory" in Al-Taiziyah is a production site for goods, not a military installation.

The Saudi air force has now struck an oil company station in Bajil, Hodeidah (three civilians injured), five times struck the empty Al-Jawf desert, and now a factory in Al-Taiziyah. The pattern is the same across all three: the Saudi air force cannot find the armed forces, so it bombs what the population depends on. The factory is the livelihood. The oil station is the fuel. The desert is the message.

The Lahij Breakthrough: The Turbah-Aden Road

Ansar Allah forces captured a series of strategic peaks and ridges in Lahij, advancing south of Al-Maqaterah toward Al-Mudaribah and Tur Al-Bahah, with gains along the Turbah-Aden road.

Trace the line. Al-Maqaterah was captured days ago, placing the Aden–Lahij road under fire control. The advance now runs south through Al-Mudaribah to Tur Al-Bahah at roughly 13.13°N 44.35°E. The Turbah-Aden road is the artery that connects Turbah (13.21°N 44.02°E) to Aden (12.83°N 45.03°E).

This is not a raid. It is a southward advance along the main supply corridor of the Saudi-UAE-backed forces. Tur Al-Bahah sits astride the junction where the road from Taiz meets the road to Aden. Whoever holds Tur Al-Bahah holds the junction. The Giants Brigades withdrew toward Tur Al-Bahah and Aden days ago. The Yemeni forces are following them to the junction.

A Giants Brigades Division General Killed. A Brigade Commander Critically Injured.

The Giants Brigades is the UAE-built, UAE-funded, UAE-commanded formation. It was recruited from the Al-Haddad and Al-Rayyan networks, trained by Emirati officers, equipped with Emirati vehicles, and deployed under Emirati direction in Aden, Shabwa, and the western coast.

A division general killed and a brigade commander critically wounded in a single engagement is command decapitation. A division general in the Giants Brigades is not a tribal sheikh with a title. He is a professional officer commanding thousands of men under Emirati supervision.

The UAE built the Giants Brigades as its instrument in southern Yemen. That instrument just lost a division commander and nearly lost a brigade commander on the Turbah-Aden road. Abu Dhabi is reading the same report Anwar Gargash was responding to when he said "confidence has been shaken."

🇱🇧 Lebanon: The Systematic Depopulation of the South

Israeli airstrikes on Kfartibnit, Aita Al-Jabal, and Al-Qusayr. Artillery shelling on Wadi Al-Salouqi, Wadi Al-Hujair, Wadi Zibqine, Al-Mansouri, the outskirts of Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, Kfartibnit, Mays Al-Jabal, the outskirts of Baraashit, the outskirts of Mayfadoun, Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah, Ainatha, the outskirts of Majdal Selm, Hadatha, and Kounin. Explosions in Beit Yahoun, Al-Tiri, Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah, and Bani Hayyan.

Count the towns. Fourteen artillery targets in one day.

The target list is not a military campaign. It is a map of the villages of southern Lebanon. Wadi Al-Salouqi, Wadi Al-Hujair, and Wadi Zibqine are the three valleys that run from the border toward the Litani. Mays Al-Jabal, Kfartibnit, Aita Al-Jabal, and Bani Hayyan sit on the front line of the 2024 ground incursion. Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah, and Hadatha sit deeper inside the country.

The pattern is the same as Gaza: strike every structure, in every village, until the population leaves. The objective is not to kill a fighter in a building. The objective is to make the village uninhabitable so that the population migrates north and the border zone becomes empty of Lebanese.

That is the hidden file. The ceasefire that was supposed to end the 2024 war is being used as a cover for the depopulation of the south. The entity is not clearing Hezbollah from the border. It is clearing the Lebanese from the border.

🇸🇾 Syria: The Ground Incursion at Al-Asbah

Israeli military forces entered Al-Asbah village in the southern Quneitra countryside with five military vehicles.

Al-Asbah sits at approximately 33.03°N 35.85°E, in the Quneitra governorate, near the 1974 disengagement line. This is a ground incursion into Syrian territory outside the buffer zone, by five armored vehicles, in daylight.

The pattern is incremental annexation. Every week, a village is entered. Every week, the vehicles go a little deeper. Every week, the Syrian government issues a statement and does nothing. The Makkah Pact that Damascus is "evaluating" contains no clause on the Golan, no mechanism to confront Israel, and no obligation to defend Quneitra.

Damascus is being entered by Israeli vehicles while it weighs a defense pact that does not name the invader.

🇮🇶 Iraq: The Turkish Drone Joins the American Package

Five MQ-9 Reapers, one MQ-1 Predator, one KC-130, and one Turkish-made AKINCI drone violated Iraqi airspace. The flights traced to bases in Jordan and Turkiye.

The Turkish AKINCI is the new information.

Until now, the air incursions were American, launched from Jordan. The AKINCI is Turkish manufactured by Baykar, the company run by Selçuk Bayraktar, son-in-law of President Erdoğan. Türkiye is a NATO member. Turkish drones were used by Azerbaijan against Armenia and by Ukraine against Russia. Now a Turkish AKINCI is over Iraqi airspace alongside American Reapers.

The launch base in Türkiye is the tell. The Incirlik Air Base at 37.00°N 35.42°E hosts US aircraft. The Diyarbakır Air Base at 37.89°N 40.20°E hosts Turkish drones. If the AKINCI launched from Diyarbakır and is operating over Iraq alongside American Reapers, Turkish and American air power are being integrated over Iraqi territory.

Türkiye is not a neutral mediator. It is a participant in the air architecture over Iraq, alongside the United States, using NATO and domestically produced platforms.

The count: eight aircraft in one day. Five of them armed Reapers. All from Jordan and Turkiye. The Iraqi government's protests have not stopped a single flight.

The Gulf: The Refueling Package Is a Strike Package

US air and naval activity intensified over the Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman. Observed:

•· Five refueling aircraft: KC-135 and KC-46A
•· One MQ-4C Triton- high-altitude maritime surveillance drone
•· One P-8A Poseidon- anti-submarine and maritime patrol aircraft
•· E-3G Sentry- AWACS, airborne early warning and control
•· E-11A- Battlefield Airborne Communications Node
•· Two additional refueling aircraft departed from Tel Aviv

Read the package as a set. It is not a patrol.

Tankers are what you surge when you need to keep strike aircraft on station for extended periods. Five tankers plus two more from Tel Aviv is a sustained air campaign package. The KC-46A is the newest US tanker, its presence indicates the deployment is not a short-notice rotation but a planned operation.

The E-3G Sentry is the airborne command and control node. It was in the air over Saudi Arabia. The Sentry does not fly over friendly territory in peacetime. It flies when an air battle is being managed.

The E-11A is the communications node that ties the aircraft together. It was also over Saudi Arabia. E-11A plus E-3G plus five tankers is the command-and-control spine of a strike campaign.

The MQ-4C Triton is the maritime surveillance platform that tracks ships. It was over the Gulf of Oman. The Triton is searching the water for Iranian naval vessels, for the enforcement units of the IRGC Navy, for the tankers transiting unauthorized routes.

The P-8A Poseidon is the anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare platform. It was also over the Gulf of Oman. The Poseidon's presence indicates the US is hunting Iranian submarines and fast attack craft.

Two refueling aircraft departed from Tel Aviv.

That is the buried information. Israeli aircraft are being refueled in the same package as US aircraft. The US and Israel are operating a joint air bridge over the Gulf. The aircraft departing Tel Aviv are being integrated into the same command architecture as the aircraft over Saudi Arabia.

The package is a preparation. It is not the strike itself. But the refueling aircraft, the AWACS, the communications node, the maritime surveillance, and the joint Israeli participation are the signature of a force that is ready to launch.

Iran: The MQM-170 Interceptions and the Starlink Answer

The IRGC Aerospace Force intercepted two American MQM-170 reconnaissance drones south of Qeshm Island using electronic warfare systems. The interceptions bring the total of MQM-170 drones seized to four.

The MQM-170 is the BQM-170 / MQM-170 Outlaw, a target drone manufactured by Griffon Aerospace, used by the US military as a maneuverable, recoverable target for air defense training and testing. It is also used as an expendable reconnaissance platform and as a decoy to trigger enemy air defenses.

Capturing four MQM-170s is not a small matter. Each drone carries avionics, a datalink, and a flight control system. Four captured units is a technology transfer on the scale of the RQ-170 Sentinel capture in 2011. The IRGC is now in possession of four American reconnaissance drones that it can study, reverse-engineer, and exploit.

The interception method is the second file. The IRGC used electronic warfare not missiles to bring the drones down. That means the IRGC has the capability to jam the MQM-170's control link and its navigation system. If the IRGC can jam the MQM-170, it can jam other US drones that use the same frequency bands and navigation protocols.

The IRGC air defense intercepted a drone that entered the airspace of Mahshahr.

Mahshahr sits at 30.55°N 49.20°E, at the head of the Persian Gulf, in Khuzestan province. It hosts the Bandar Imam Petrochemical Complex, the largest petrochemical facility in Iran. A drone entering Mahshahr airspace is a drone approaching the petrochemical complex the economic heart of the province.

The IRGC intercepted it. That is the fourth interception in the last several days.

Explosions on Qeshm Island. Explosions in Bandar Lengeh.

Qeshm Island at 26.85°N 55.95°E was struck by US aircraft on 29 October. Explosions were reported there again, with unconfirmed reports that an air-defense platform was targeted by American strikes.

Bandar Lengeh sits at 26.55°N 54.88°E, on the Iranian coast west of Qeshm. Explosions were reported there, cause unknown.

The pattern: the US is conducting suppression of enemy air defenses (SEAD) operations over the Strait of Hormuz. The Qeshm air-defense platform is the target. The Bandar Lengeh explosions may be a second SEAD strike.

The US is preparing the air defense environment for a larger campaign. The refueling package, the AWACS, the SEAD strikes on Qeshm, and the drone incursions are all part of the same preparation.

The Iranian Army announced a missile launch exercise in eastern Iran.

Eastern Iran is the Khorasan region the border with Afghanistan and Pakistan. A missile exercise there is a signal to Pakistan and to the US bases in the region. The exercise is timed to the Chinese Special Envoy's visit and to the Doha talks.

The National Cyberspace Center offers Starlink control technology to "like-minded countries."

The head of Iran's National Cyberspace Center said Iran is prepared to share technology for controlling Starlink with like-minded countries. He said that if Iran decides to move from monitoring to controlling Starlink, it would be able to do so using the technology.

This is the answer to the Youngrud operation. The 10 Starlink terminals seized in western Iran were the first confirmation that the US is using Starlink to coordinate covert networks. Now Iran is saying it has moved from monitoring to controlling meaning jamming, spoofing, or intercepting the Starlink signal.

The offer to share the technology with "like-minded countries" is a signal to Russia, China, and the Global South. Iran is offering a counter-Starlink capability to any state that wants to prevent the US from using satellite internet to run covert operations inside its territory.

The vessel struck off Lima, Oman.

UKMTO reported an incident approximately 9 nautical miles northeast of Lima, Oman. The master reported the vessel was struck by an unidentified projectile, causing a hole on the starboard side.

Lima sits at 26.38°N 56.47°E, on the Musandam peninsula, at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz. Nine nautical miles northeast of Lima is inside the Strait of Hormuz, on the Omani side.

The vessel was struck by a projectile. That is the Iranian enforcement regime extending to the Omani side of the strait. The tanker was on an unauthorized route. The projectile was the enforcement.

The Indian Navy rescued the Iranian fishing vessel Al-Azeeni.

The Indian Navy secured the Iranian fishing vessel Al-Azeeni, rescued all 20 crew members, and arrested suspected pirates. The vessel had been hijacked off Somalia on 29 October and was approaching the shipping corridor south of Socotra Island.

This is the corridor defense file. India is protecting the sea lane south of Socotra the same corridor that the INSTC and the Chabahar port connect to. The Indian Navy is operating in the Gulf of Aden and the Arabian Sea to protect the shipping that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz.

The pirates are the cover. The real operation is India securing the corridor that connects Chabahar to the Indian Ocean. The Iranian fishing vessel was the pretext. The Indian Navy was already there, waiting.

The bill.

Six fronts, one day. A factory in Taiz. A Giants Brigades general dead on the Turbah-Aden road. Fourteen villages shelled in southern Lebanon. Israeli vehicles in Quneitra. A Turkish AKINCI over Iraq with American Reapers. Seven tankers and AWACS over the Gulf with two refuelers from Tel Aviv. Four MQM-170s captured by electronic warfare. SEAD strikes on Qeshm. A missile exercise in the east. A Starlink control offer to the Global South. A projectile hole off Lima. An Indian Navy rescue south of Socotra.

The war is not one front. It is a ledger with six columns, and every column is being written in the same hour.

text:
People say nations are warning them to prepare.  Fine.  Let's look at preparation through the lens of an experienced survivor.

Here are a few random topics.

What an expedition professional keeps around for survival, and tips:

1:  The survivalist's myth.

I restock my supply of MREs regularly.  They do not last forever, and you're best eating them in three years and buying more.

I keep enough to survive for three months, but it must be noted that I don't eat much, to begin with, and I am very experienced in conserving calories.

MREs are not the Holy Grail of survival.  They are varied and contain many nutrients.  They exist to power a warrior for a limited time and keep his morale reasonable.

They are not easy to pack out, as they take up lots of room.  You can't carry many days of MREs, when traveling solo.  Buy enough, but focus elsewhere.

You don't keep these around to live on exclusively.  You keep them around for convenience and variety, to take a break from what you'll probably consider bland.

Do not rely on your car or SUV to carry your supplies.  Assume you will abandon it and travel on foot.  If you have a pickup, you've effectively got a sedan with no trunk, and someone will steal them.

2:  What the world lives on:

I store lots of dried red beans and rice, which I triple seal in individual meal-sized bags, and then pack into larger bags for convenience.

A substantial portion of the world lives exclusively on those two things, and you can, too.  They also happen to last a very, very long time in dried form.

It is best to sift, shake, and dust them before packaging, and wear gloves, when doing so, to prevent contaminants.  That said, nobody else does.

These don't carry every single nutrient your doctor says you need, but neither does what you're eating now.  You'll be fine.  Keep a significant supply, on hand.

All that low wage and slave labor on Earth?  This is what they're eating, and they do more work in a day than you do in a month.

It's also what I mostly eat when I'm out there.  It will keep your stomach full and your back strong for whatever you'll need to do, and it doesn't take up much room.

3:  The things that change the game.

Always keep a healthy supply of salt and whole peppercorns around.  Salt is a rock, and it never goes bad.  Consider how much you think you need, and triple it.

Whole peppercorns last an incredibly long time, as well; a ridiculously long time, in fact.  Still, buy them in vacuum-sealed bags.  You can get them online, like that.

The same rule applies with pepper.  Triple what you think you'll need.  You will need to grind these.  Buy a pepper grinder.  It's the easy way to grind them.

You should have one, anyway.  Don't use dust on food.  Only use fresh ground.  It's night and day.  Don't let a guest show up at your house and serve them dust.

Keep a mortar and pestle around the house in case your grinder breaks.  Ceramic is the best material for both, but it can be expensive.  Spring for it if you can.

If you need to pack out, make sure you have a very small pepper grinder, to save calories crushing peppercorns.  If that breaks, you'll be crushing them with the flat of a knife or hatchet.

Salt and peppercorns may seem a luxury, and carrying a small grinder may seem an inefficient use of cargo capacity, but they make everything better, which is important, when you have less than you did, before.

Do not neglect those two things.  I am notorious for packing annoyingly light even on vehicle dependent expeditions, and even I always have salt and pepper.

4:  Supplemental food supplies.

As long as you've got the space of a house, to play with, it's important to consider including various protein bars and meal replacement bars.  They are small, and can keep you going for a while.

Attempt to find those with many nutrients that last a long time.  They won't taste as good as others, but you'll get used to it in a couple of weeks, and be fine.

These are incredibly useful because you can stock the dead space in a pack with them.  You're always going to have voids, not matter how carefully you pack.  Use those voids productively.

I have no specific suggestions, for the type you should choose, as the options are incredibly varied.  I myself just look for long life and nutrients.  Don't skimp on these, but also don't let them go bad.

Eat the things before that happens.  What you'll be using them for are times when you need a jolt of nutrients and calories, and to break up the rest of your diet.

5:  Brawndo.  It's got electrolytes.

Water is important, but so is Brawndo.  Keep some Gatorade powder and electrolyte powder around.  watch the expiration dates, though.  Cycle through them as needed.

Be aware that true electrolyte powder tastes and smells rancid, so balance flavor in relation to content.  It won't do you any good if you don't consume it, or if it makes you miserable.

You want to ensure that at least one serving of water, to be considered one gallon, includes at least electrolyte powder or Gatorade powder.

It's normally wasteful to do this but, when stocking electrolyte powder, attempt to buy it in individually packaged servings.  This not only preserves the supply, but it prevents you from losing track of intake.

Your Gatorade powder won't last forever, and it's really more of a solution for when your at home, so keep an eye on expiration dates and use it before it goes bad.

6:  Water, part 1.

Consider your water intake.  The human body requires a certain amount, so study it carefully, and be aware that you are not as good at preventing sweat and generally surviving hot weather environments as I am.

The more you sweat, the more you need, so learning how to conserve calories and training your body to function more efficiently will reduce your intake requirements.

That means staying in shape, and functioning on proper nutrients but reduced calorie intake until your metabolism adapts.  Your doctor may say this is a bad idea, your AI may say it's impossible.

They are both incorrect.  They have never survived extreme environments unsupported when things go wrong, and neither have most survivalist blog writers or  YouTube creators.  Following their advice is lethal.

They don't know what they are talking about.  Manufacture yourself into a machine from 200,000 years ago.  You don't have to eat nuts.  You have to be able to survive on less then you can right now.

Water is something you cannot train, but what you can do is train your body and mind to waste less of it, thus reducing intake requirements.  Learn to use fewer calories, sweat less, and you will be better off.

7:  Water, part 2.

It is advisable to store as much water as reasonable around the house, but you need to cycle through it.  The expiration date on the water bottle isn't for the water.  It's for the plastic, but things do grow in water.

If you can boil it and transfer it into glass containers, you'll be much better off, but that doesn't have to happen.  When you buy water, however, buy it in big, sealed containers.

Individual water bottles should be kept around, but they are an incredible waste of space, and you can't keep as much around.  They are also more expensive.

That said, I advise buying a few cartons of Smart Water bottles.  It's no better than normal water aside from flavor, but the bottles themselves last a long time and seal well.  They may be of use, in time.

You will also want to keep a few buckets and plastic wrap around, as well as a large plastic bin.  The second things look like something will go wrong, fill them up drop in a purification tablet (will be discussed) and seal them with plastic wrap.

The water in them can be used to cause toilets to function, to wash your face and hands, which is important, and simply to drink until you reach the point at which you tap your other supplies.

8:  Water, part 3.

Now we get into the section discussing how to purify your water, and where to source it.  First up is purification, and the most important thing is a filter.

I personally own a Ketadyn Pocket.  It is expensive, but it is built to last, and to protect it's filter elements.  If an impact flexes the housing of a water filter, it can damage that element.

This specific model can be rebuilt, maintained, and the filter elements last so long most will never need to change them, but keep spares on hand, anyway.

Ketadyn also offers an improved model, which I will buy, soon.  While the pocket will filter nearly anything that matters, their improved unit will also handle much tinier microorganisms, but it is not made of metal.

When traveling the world, that Pocket has served me very well.  It is not perfect, though.  That is what the improved model is for.  I would suggest purchasing both.  The Pocket for general use, and the other for when things become extremely questionable.

Filters aren't everything, though.

To help ensure you're going to be fine, when things are particularly nasty, or to purify large amounts of water quickly when you really have to watch calorie use, make sure you have purification tablets, on hand.

They don't take up much room, so stock as many as you can, within reason.  They can be expensive, and I strongly suggest purchasing them through a reputable filter manufacturer.

I keep things a little varied, but I make sure I can pack out enough for three months, minus water.  I have a very effective filter, for water, and purifying tablets, as well.

That's not where this stops.

Boiling is absolutely critical for long-term survival, for making those beans and rice, and also for purifying water.  You will find later that there is a balance you will have to strike.

You will want a lightweight, durable container in which to boil water, and preferably a way to cover it to avoid some of the evaporation.  I suggest titanium for weight savings, later on.

Consider Snow Peak brand products, for this purpose.  They are expensive.  They are the Gucci of the overland crowd, and most Expedition professionals roll our eyes at their enthusiasts, but none of us will turn our nose up at a lightweight pot.

What buying from them ensures is high quality titanium alloy.  If you cheap out, you will likely be getting lower quality materials.  This is important.  Buy it once, and buy it for life.

Be aware that you will need to practice cooking with titanium.  It will burn things very quickly, so you'll have to stir more frequently than you would with a material that is more dense, but it's a lot easier to carry.

9:  From home to beyond:  Electricity.

During disasters and emergencies in the civilian and non-traveling world, you are most likely to be stuck at home.  That is a very, very important thing to think about.

The objective, when surviving at home, is to step down the ladder of luxury as luxuries run dry.  That means to use your normal equipment as long as you can for food and boiling.

As long as power remains functional, there's no reason to stop using any electricity.  Use it all you like, and as much as you can.  You're trying to conserve survival resources.

When that electricity ceases to function, you've got two paths ahead of you:  You can use your generator alternate between cooking food, and charging/refrigeration/entertainment/connectivity.

You can also use it exclusively for everything but cooking.  What you're doing is picking a path, and you need to consider whether or not you will need to travel.

Another choice is to use it only to keep devices and various batteries charged.  All devices need to remain charged at all times, even if that means using solar, which you should have.

Regardless:

The fuel your generator uses is fuel your vehicle could be using.  All fuel should be identical and, therefore, all fuel equates to one total supply volume.

Every quart you use in that generator is another quart you can't use in your vehicle.  Use that generator wisely.  If it will power a microwave, that is a very efficient way to cook with electricity.

Beyond all the generator talk, there is that previously mentioned solar factor.  Buy a decent set of compact panels that can be deployed that will actually charge something quickly, as well as a very compact expandable panel to carry.

9:  From home to beyond:  Cooking.

This is where the luxury ladder really comes into play.  While your generator is at least keeping your normal food from spoiling, you may also be using it to cook.  There will be a point at which this must stop.

After two days, if you still haven't received news that a disaster is over or that power will be restored soon, it's time to stop wasting fuel, and use it only to keep food from spoiling.

Now you're on to propane.

You should have a propane grill.  It should be a Weber Q model, specifically.  Those are the most efficient grills on the market, easy to operate, incredibly even heating, and probably the best cooking possible.

Buy the 40 pound tank adapter for it.

At all times, it is desirable to have two to four forty pound propane tanks full and in good condition stored safely.  You may live in a condition in which that is not possible, such as in an apartment.

If you live in such a condition, there may still be a way to keep them.  Ask your neighbors, and see if there is a safe storage location available, or merely a place they can be suitably hidden outside of the building's confines.

If you live in a separate house or a condominium that allows such storage, however, there is no problem.  Simply store them safely.  You will need them.  Propane is your next step down the ladder.

When you've stopped using electricity to cook, you will now be using propane to accomplish the same.  Use it as long as you stay in that location.  You can carry a Weber Q and propane in a vehicle, if required, but your vehicle may become useless.

So, while you're at home after electricity needs to be conserved extensively, cook and boil with propane.  Two tanks will outlast most disasters and weather events.  Four tanks will take you very, very far.  Be miserly with them, and stretch out their use.

The charcoal step.

Next up, if you have such a grill, you will be moving to charcoal.  Ensure you can ignite it without lighter fluid.  You should already know how to do this.  Practice, but do keep that fluid around, so if you have trouble, you don't burn extra calories trying.

Charcoal is not an efficient store of energy, as propane is.  Don't keep sixteen tons of it around, as it's more of a hazard than a propane tank is.  Keep as much as the grilling enthusiast next door has on hand.

I personally don't bother with this step, but owning an actual charcoal grill is advised, for efficiency in the next step.  I strongly suggest a Weber Smoky Joe compact unit or it's larger traditional twin.

We come to the final, perpetual option.

You need to learn to build a fire.  To make it a bit easier, buy a few of those magnesium fire starters.  They're cheap, and they do work, but that's not step one.

Step one is owning a bunch of Bic lighters.  They're cheap, they take up very little space, and you can pack out many of them if the need arises.  They also last a long time.

Keep wood split and ready at all times.  When you pick up sticks, in your yard, keep them, break off the little twigs, and separate them.  You'll need both, to have an easy time of things.

If you order many things from Amazon, break down the boxes and keep them somewhere they won't be a fire hazard.  Cardboard, once ignited, will burn hot and for a relatively long time; helping to start the fire.

There are various orders in which you can manage starting fires.  Keep in mind whether or not you will need to travel, of course, but retain your calories.

Do it the easy way, first, while still retaining enough Bic lighters to keep it easy when you end up on foot after your vehicle becomes useless if you have to leave.

Fire starting cubes or bricks are very helpful, as well, but these must be stored as carefully as charcoal, and kept sealed from the elements.  A Ziploc bag is sufficient, most of the time.  I double them up in two directions, and tape over the open ends.

Eventually, you'll be down to those magnesium fire starters, so learn how to use them, as well as traditional methods of starting fires.  Be very careful with Youtube tutorials.  Those people are often fools.

There are many different ways to use each method, and you're after the laziest, quickest way possible, in order to conserve calories.

10:  I've been rambling, so here is strong advice.

The thing you need to internalize the most is to build up a non-lazy body that can survive on less and doesn't sweat as much doing normal things, and then be lazy as hell.

Survival is about conserving calories and avoiding sweating, as that conserves everything else you've got.

Always find an easy way to do things, and use it as long as you can, before working down to the more difficult ways.

There are many different subjects I could address, but I'm going to end up saving that for a book, unless the world ends between now and then.

The way everyone's talking, you'd think an alien invasion was on the horizon.  Still, if you've read this, you've learned a few things.

So, be happy.

THE HIGH PRIEST OF A NEW COVENANT

1 Now the main point of what we are saying is this: We do have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven, 2 and who serves in the sanctuary, the true tabernacle set up by th eLord, not by a merre human being.

3 Every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices, and so it was necessary for this one also to have something to offer. 4 If he were on earth, he would not be a priest, for there are already priests who offer the gifts prescribed by the law.

5 They serve at a sanctuary that is a copy and shadow of what is in heaven. This is why Moses was warned when he was about to build the tabernacle: "See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain."

6 But in fact the ministry Jesus has received is as superior to theirs as the covenant of which he is mediator is superior to the old one, since the new covenant is established on better promises.

Hebrews 8:1-6

Key points I take away from this:

* Jesus, as our high priest, sits at the right hand of the Father and serves in the sanctuary of heaven set up by the Most High God himself

* Jesus is the only priest in heaven assigned on our behalf

* The old line of priests given to the tribes under Moses served in a human made sanctuary that resembled the one in heaven; one made according to the directions given to Moses

* Jesus's sanctuary and ministry is superior to the old one, as are also His gifts and sacrifice, and of course, His covenant

* This is why the old covenant is no longer the one we use to have our relationship with God. Nor is an earthly temple needed to perform the duties of the high priest. 

* With Jesus as our high priest, our sanctuary is in heaven and our bodies are filled with the Holy Spirit after accepting this truth, thus making our bodies a living temple where God dwells within us as he did behind the curtain in the Holy of Holies.

text:
The plane crashed because the 55 year old experienced white dude pilot (who i wouldn't worry about on sight) made a risky and fatal decision. Yes even experienced pilots can make poor decisions. 
There is a captain and a first officer.
The captain makes all final decisions.
He was warned by ATC of the "pretty nasty" weather and "moderate to extreme precipitation" 10 mins prior and made a risky decision for only a slight deviation that turned out to be fatal. 
It was on the radio, 10 mins prior. You can find the audio. ATC offered them a route around. The captain made a slight deviation because it wasn't serious and they were above the storm until that cell ballooned up from 33000 ft to 48000 ft ceiling in a few minutes and by then it was too late for them to climb out of it.
From grok:
The earlier ATC exchange you’re remembering does exist. It comes from Miami Center (ZMA) LiveATC archives and covers the period roughly 10–15 minutes before the final mayday (around 12:36–12:37 p.m. EST while the jet was still ~80 miles / ~8 minutes from the cell it later entered). It is not in the short final-minute clips that circulate most widely, but it appears in longer reconstructions and analyses (especially MyRadar/Matthew Cappucci’s weather note and some YouTube breakdowns that pull the earlier sector recordings).
Key excerpts from the earlier exchange (paraphrased/transcribed from public LiveATC-based sources)
Around the time the jet was descending from FL410 toward FL350 and crossing into Florida airspace:
ATC cleared N722BD direct to Freeport and warned that the turn/route “looks pretty nasty.”
Controller described a large area of moderate-to-extreme precipitation (roughly 100 miles in diameter, reported in the 11 o’clock position ~25 miles ahead in one reconstruction).
Crew (captain’s voice in the analysis) said something to the effect of “[we] may need a slight left deviation for that weather up ahead.”
ATC approved weather deviations: “deviations left and right are approved… Freeport when able.”
The aircraft took a left deviation. At that point they were still well clear of the specific rapidly growing cell they later entered near Royal Palm Beach/Wellington.
MyRadar’s summary of the same period (Matthew Cappucci) states exactly this sequence and notes the storm cell was still building dramatically (tops rising from ~33,000 ft to ~48,000 ft in ~20 minutes). The crew continued after the advisory and deviation approval rather than requesting a major reroute farther north or south.
Later (starting ~12:45–12:47 p.m., now at FL350 and closer to the cell), the familiar short segment begins:
Light clear ice (manageable), moderate turbulence (±600–700 ft), OAT –47 °C, direct Freeport.
Request for a better ride.
ATC: ride should improve in their airspace; better rides ahead.
Crew: now picking up precipitation; request climb to FL370 (approved).
Within ~20–30 seconds: mayday, descending 8–10k then 20k+ fpm, overspeed, 60° bank, “we’re going to crash into the ground,” “out of time.”
Where to find the audio
YouTube searches for “N722BD ATC” or “Full ATC Audio Learjet Final 5 Minutes” (e.g., the InterTainment video covering ~5 min 48 s of Miami Center, and VASAviation’s weather-focused edit). Some of these include or reference the earlier deviation/“pretty nasty” portion.
https://t.co/tYrZZmE8tv archives for Miami Center (ZMA) frequencies around 17:30–17:50 UTC on 1 Nov 2026. The final segment is on ~125.325 MHz; the earlier weather/deviation talk was on a prior sector.
Detailed weather + ATC timeline: MyRadar MetNote on N722BD (Matthew Cappucci).
No official NTSB transcript has been released yet—these are reconstructions from public LiveATC recordings. The audio of the final minute is widely available but extremely distressing; the earlier portion is calmer but still relevant to the weather-avoidance decisions.

text:
US Elections Thread 2/5 (Financials) 

Options markets are generally pricing in a non-event for financials during the election. A few quantamental teams / desks believe (and we agree) that the upside of REPUBLICAN SWEEP is underappreciated. 

A Democratic Congress would slow the next round of financial deregulation. In crypto, it would be harder to pass legislation clarifying SEC/CFTC jurisdiction and expanding regulated trading around perpetual futures and prediction markets, reducing the upside from new products for $HOOD and hyperliquid:native. 

For banks, Democrats are more likely to resist further capital relief and scrutinize softer stress tests, limiting additional buybacks and balance-sheet growth that benefit capital-intensive trading and lending businesses. 

REPUBLICAN SWEEP (5%)
$HOOD: +1% to +3%
hyperliquid:native: +4% to +8%
$C: +0.5% to +1.25%

DEMOCRATS SWEEP (75%) 
Expected, flat   

DIVIDED CONGRESS (20%) 
Expected, flat

$HOOD: DISTRIBUTION + PERMISSIONS

Robinhood already has good product + distribution, so deregulation allows for the offering perpetual futures, event contracts, and other highly profitable trading products to eligible customers. That makes HOOD an efficient expression of broader retail derivatives access. 

Using the $300m quarterly event/crypto revenue base as a scale reference, an EXTRA persistent 10–20% revenue uplift, at assumed 40–60% incremental pretax margins and 25% tax, adds roughly $35–100m annual net profit. Valuing that at 25–35 times, allowing 1–2 years for delivery and using a roughly $75bn equity reference produces the working price band.

hyperliquid:native: DISTRIBUTION + PERMISSIONS

The exposure here is similar to HOOD except even more sensitive to regulatory pressures. A Republican win does not automatically authorize U.S. access to Hyperliquid but the token moves on sentiment before  economics. 

Recall that a favorable Trump mention triggered a 14% rally by signaling political acceptance and drawing speculative flows. That makes the near-term election trade more about impacts to sentiment. 

$C: BALANCE-SHEET CAPACITY

Citi is interesting because a scheduled regulatory change could force it to retain more shareholder capita and Republican deregulation could reduce that burden.

Banks fund their loans and trading positions with a mix of deposits, borrowing and shareholders’ equity. Regulators require a minimum amount of equity to absorb losses.

Under current rules, Citi’s mandatory equity requirement rises from $11.60 to $12.10 for every $100 of risk-weighted assets in January 2028. A higher requirement means more future profit must stay inside the bank rather than fund buybacks. 

Republican-backed regulatory reform could soften that increase and Republican control of Congress would give that agenda more political support, although regulators can change capital rules without new legislation.

Avoiding the full half-percentage-point increase would create roughly $6.2bn of capital flexibility at Citi’s existing asset base, about 3% of its market value. The same hypothetical reduction represents around 2.6% at BAC, 1.5% at Goldman and 1.2% at JPMorgan.

text:
Strong crossovers exist. Your proposed product changes for Grok Bot efficiency are a practical, productized application of Elon Musk’s 5-step algorithm (Question → Delete → Simplify → Accelerate → Automate, in that fixed order) to the problem of AI agent/routine cost and usage.17
Direct mappings
•Question every requirement (make it less dumb): Smarter defaults that force the slowest practical schedule + narrowest trigger, plus pre-save cost estimates/warnings and usage thresholds that surface the top draining routines. This makes users confront whether a frequent/broad run is actually needed instead of defaulting to always-on.15
•Delete: The one-click efficiency audit that lists high-cost routines and offers pause, convert-to-skill, or remove options. The “Make it cheaper” button and Efficiency Mode (prefer skills over always-on, connectors over computer use) are deletion mechanisms. Musk’s rule of thumb is that if you don’t add ~10% back later, you didn’t delete enough—these tools make that easy to test.17
•Simplify (only after deletion): Built-in “Only run if something changed” toggle, favoring skills, and reducing noisy group-chat activity. These strip complexity from triggers and execution so only necessary work remains.
•Accelerate: Less direct, but tighter defaults + change-detection shorten effective cycle time by eliminating wasted runs, and the audit surfaces optimizations that speed up what survives.
•Automate last: The product itself handles the change-detection check, cost guidance, and audit suggestions so users don’t manually invent the patterns. Efficiency Mode applies the lighter defaults automatically. This matches the “automate only after questioning, deleting, and simplifying” rule.18
Key differences
Musk’s algorithm is a general first-principles process for any system (rockets, factories, code, personal workflows). Your proposals are a specific UX layer that embeds the same sequence into Grok Bot’s routine/scheduling product so efficient behavior becomes the default path rather than something users must study and apply manually. The recent X post framing Musk’s algorithm as a Grok prompt is related but separate—it is an advisory system prompt for the model; your suggestions are product features that would make the algorithm’s principles operational for cost control.12
Overall, the proposals align closely with the algorithm’s core insight that most waste comes from automating or optimizing things that should have been questioned and deleted first. They would reduce the need for users to apply the algorithm themselves while still preserving control.

          The origin of truth... @TransientLabs 

     Origin of truth...Apple origin : 

The rugged mountain slopes of the Tian Shan range in Kazakhstan.
Wild Ancestor: 
    The wild species Malus sieversii is the direct ancestor of the modern cultivated apple.
Spread: 
    Ancient traders and animals carried the seeds along the Silk Road.
Genetics: 
    Modern DNA studies prove that most cultivated apples trace their roots back to these Kazakh forests.
Wild Ancestor: 
      The tough and sweet Malus sieversii is the primary genetic parent of nearly all modern apples.
Almaty's Name: 
     The largest city in Kazakhstan, Almaty, translates to "father of apples" or "full of apples".
Early Spread: 
     Bears and birds first carried the seeds, and human traders along the Silk Road later spread them toward Europe and Asia.
    The apple of discord (lesser known myths,Greek mythology)
    The apple of discord is a Greek mythology tale where Eris, the goddess of chaos, tossed a golden apple inscribed "To the fairest" into a royal wedding. It sparked a fierce quarrel among three goddesses Hera, Athena, and Aphrodite that led directly to the Trojan War.
The Wedding and the Golden Apple The Snub: 
     The sea goddess Thetis and her husband Peleus held a grand wedding. They did not invite Eris, the goddess of strife, because she only brought fights and bad moods.
The Revenge:
      Mad about the slight, Eris crashed the party anyway. She threw a bright golden apple onto the banquet table.
      The Inscription: Words were carved into the apple that said " Kalliste" or "To the fairest "
The Fight of the Goddesses The Claims:
     Three powerful goddesses immediately wanted the apple: Hera (queen of the gods), Athena (goddess of wisdom), and Aphrodite (goddess of love).The Deadlock: No other god dared to say who was the best or most beautiful, as picking one meant making the other two enemies for life.
The Choice: 
      Zeus refused to pick, so he sent them to a young shepherd and prince of Troy named Paris.

The Judgment of Paris The Bribes: 

    The goddesses tried to buy his vote. Hera promised him supreme power and control over Asia. Athena promised him glory and skill in every battle. Aphrodite made the best offer: she promised him Helen, the most beautiful mortal woman alive.The Winner: Paris gave the golden apple to Aphrodite.

     The Result The Abduction: Paris sailed to Sparta and won Helen away from her husband, King Menelaus. Some versions say she fell in love with him, while others say Aphrodite used magic.
     The War: When Paris took Helen back to Troy, the angry Greek kings joined forces under Agamemnon and sailed to attack Troy, starting a ten year war....

More known religious concepts about the apple:
    In the Book of Genesis, the forbidden fruit in the Garden of Eden is only called peri, a generic Hebrew word for "fruit". The popular idea that Eve ate an apple comes from a Latin wordplay in the 4th century and old European art.

The Real Biblical StoryThe Rule: 
      God told Adam and Eve they could eat from any tree in the garden except one. That was the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. The Test: A talking serpent tempted Eve. It told her she would not die, but would become like God. The Choice: Eve saw that the fruit looked good and wanted wisdom. She picked it, ate it, and gave some to Adam, who was with her. 
The Result: 
     Their eyes opened to their nakedness, they felt shame, and God sent them out of the garden.

How the Apple Became Famous The Latin Pun: 
       When St. Jerome translated the Bible into Latin, he used the word malum. In Latin, malum means both "evil" and an apple, like fruit. 
The Art: 
    Medieval and Renaissance painters in Europe used the familiar local apple as a symbol for sin and the forbidden fruit in their artwork...  
        Summarising: What is the concept of the apple in history religion and conceptual meaning.
    The apple is a rich symbol across human history, representing temptation and original sin in Christianity, immortality and wisdom in Greek mythology, and health or discord in secular culture, bridging ideas of desire, knowledge, and mortality for thousands of years.
Religion and Myth Forbidden Fruit: 
    Abrahamic traditions link the apple to the tree of knowledge of good and evil in Eden, though the Bible just says "fruit."
Greek Mythology: 
    Oranges and apples mixed in tales; the Golden Apple of Discord sparked the Trojan War, and the Garden of the Hesperides held immortal apples.Norse Tradition: Goddess Idun kept golden apples that gave the Norse gods eternal youth.

History and Science Origins: 

     Wild apples started in the mountains of Central Asia.
The Silk Road: 
     Travelers carried seeds across Asia and Europe.Newton's Apple: A falling apple helped Isaac Newton think about gravity.

Conceptual Meaning Knowledge, Symbolism: 

It stands for learning, truth, and forbidden wisdom.
Temptation:
     It represents human desire and choice. Health: The old saying links eating one to good wellness.
Desire and Refreshment:
     In poetic books, the apple represents physical delight, fragrance, and comfort.
    The Myth of Temptation: Culturally, the conceptual idea of the "apple" shifted to symbolize human disobedience, the loss of innocence, and the transition from a state of pure trust to moral accountability.
      In Western art, the apple stands for the sin of Adam and Eve. Love and Beauty: Ancient Greek art links the apple to Aphrodite, the goddess of love. Life and Death: Decaying apples or apple cores represent the passing of time and human mortality (vanitas).

                       After Life...  @TransientLabs 

      The connection between apples and life after death is deeply rooted in ancient mythology, where the fruit acts as a bridge, a key and a source of rebirth across the veil of mortality. 
     Across many cultures, apples represent the food of the gods that grants immortality, meaning that to hold or eat an apple after death is to live forever. 

Here is how the apple connects the physical world to the afterlife: 

The Celtic Realm of Avalon (The Isle of Apples): 
      In Celtic mythology, the ultimate resting place for heroes and souls is Avalon, which literally translates to "The Isle of Apples." The Bridge to Afterlife: It was a mythical island paradise where apple trees were always in bloom and bore fruit year-round. Burial Ritual: The Celts frequently buried apples in graves alongside the deceased. The fruit served as a magical passport and sustained the soul, allowing lovers and families to find each other in the Next World and achieve spiritual rebirth.

 Norse Mythology:
      Iðunn’s Apples of Youth: In Norse myth, the gods are not naturally immortal; they require a specific source of life to keep them from aging and dying.Defeating Death: The goddess Iðunn (Idun) guards a casket of magical golden apples.Eternal Renewal: When the gods begin to grow old and approach the shadow of death, they eat these apples to instantly restore their youth, effectively conquering death and maintaining their eternal existence.

 Greek Mythology: 
      The Golden Apples of the Hesperides: For the ancient Greeks, the Golden Apples grew in a sacred orchard at the westernmost edge of the world, closely tied to the sunset (which symbolized the end of life).The Reward of Immortality: These apples grew on a tree given to Hera by Gaia. They granted immortality and divine status to anyone who ate them.

The Elysian Connection: 
      The garden was located near the Elysian Fields, the Greek afterlife for the virtuous. The apple represented the ultimate prize of an eternal life free from the decay of the underworld. 

The Symbolism:
     If you are connecting the apple to a couple staying together after death, the apple represents the food of eternity. While their physical bodies might perish, sharing or holding the apple ensures their souls bypass the standard decay of death, allowing them to step into an everlasting paradise together. 

     In mythology, the apple is the ultimate symbol of eternal love, fertility, and the bridge between life and death. While apples themselves grant immortality to the gods in various traditions, the specific myth about a devoted couple whose love keeps them together as intertwined trees even after death is actually the Greek myth of Philemon and Baucis.

    Though they are turned into an oak and a linden tree (rather than an apple tree), their story is deeply intertwined with the broader ancient tradition of using sacred trees and fruits, especially apples to represent a love that survives the grave.

The Ultimate Myth of love after life:
     Philemon and Baucis: In this famous story from Ovid's Metamorphoses, an impoverished, elderly couple named Philemon and Baucis unknowingly welcome the gods Zeus and Hermes into their home after all their wealthy neighbors turn them away. 

The Reward: 
     Touched by the couple’s deep hospitality and lifelong devotion to each other, Zeus offers to grant them any wish. 
The Wish:
      They ask that they may serve the gods together and, most importantly, that neither would ever have to live a day without the other or see the other's grave. The Afterlife Union: 
      When they finally reach the end of their exceptionally long lives, the gods transform them simultaneously. Philemon turns into a mighty oak tree, and Baucis into a gentle linden tree, their branches forever intertwined, allowing them to stay together for eternity.

The Apple as the Symbol of Marriage and Eternal Union: 

    While Philemon and Baucis became the oak and linden, the apple tree and its fruit carry the specific mythological weight of binding couples together in life and the afterlife:

Greek Wedding Seals:
     In ancient Greece, the primordial goddess Gaia gave an apple tree to Hera on her wedding day to Zeus, to symbolize an eternal, unbreakable union. From then on, newlywed couples in Athens would share and eat an apple before entering the bridal chamber, to ensure lasting love and fertility.

The Proposal: 
      Tossing an apple at someone was the ancient Greek equivalent of a marriage proposal. Catching it meant the recipient accepted your love and committed their life to yours. 

The Celtic Avalon (The Isle of Apples):
       In Celtic mythology, the apple is the exact bridge between love and the afterlife. The mythical paradise Avalon literally translates to the 'Isle of Apples.' It is a realm of eternal youth, where souls go after death. The Celts frequently buried apples in the graves of lovers, so they would have the food of rebirth to find each other and stay sustained in the Next World.

Brett Johnson says he made up to $160,000 a week filing fake tax returns, using dead people's identities, while he was working as an informant for the US Secret Service.

He grew up in Kentucky in a family he says ran small scams for fun. Fake insurance claims. Lies everywhere. Crime felt normal.

In the early 2000s he found the internet and built something nobody had seen before. A website where criminals from all over the world bought and sold stolen credit cards, fake IDs and hacking tools. It was called ShadowCrew.

The Secret Service later called him one of the founding fathers of modern cybercrime.

In 2004 they caught him. Then they made him an offer. Work for us. Help us catch the others.

He said yes. He sat in a government office during the day helping agents hunt hackers.

At night he says he went home and kept stealing.

In the video below, Brett explains how. He says he used the identities of dead people to file tax refunds. Thousands of them. He says at the peak the money coming in hit $160,000 a week.

He tells it with a half smile, like he still can't believe it worked.

The Secret Service eventually figured it out. He was arrested again. He escaped. He landed on the US Marshals' most wanted list before they caught him for good.

He served years in federal prison.

Today he makes his living as a cybersecurity consultant, giving talks to the same companies and agencies he used to rob.

Is Brett Johnson proof that people can really change, or the ultimate con man who found a way to get paid by both sides?

text:
Tokyo is omitting Washington's 3.5%-of-GDP defense target from its year-end security strategy, Sankei reported on 2 November. The real fear may be something else: Trump potentially meeting the leaders of China and Russia in China on 18-19 November.

As Americans vote in their midterms today, Sankei says the Takaichi government is anxious. If Republicans lose, they describe Trump as 死に体 shinitai ('lame duck'). This sumo term refers to a wrestler whose body is already past saving before he hits the sand, carrying a fatalism that the English idiom lacks. Such a president looks abroad for a legacy, and Tokyo fears he will seek it with Beijing and Moscow, bypassing Japan entirely. A senior foreign ministry official calls this prospect "not comfortable." Another government official is blunter: "If Japan-US relations go sour, it is China and Russia who profit." The 3.5% target is where the friction lies. Washington wants allies to spend that share of their economy on defense, but citing tight public finances, Tokyo will not list it as a goal for 2027 to 2031. A president hungry for wins could use that gap to squeeze Japan.

Russia has darkened the scene. On 2 November, its bombs hit a school in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region where aid was being handed out. Nine more bombs then fell on the shelter where survivors had fled, killing at least 24 people, including rescuers and police. Russia did the same in August at Kryvyi Rih, using a second strike to target those who came to help. Moscow is demonstrating that it pays little price in Washington, just weeks before it may share a table with the US in China.

Beijing is watching today's vote for a different reason. Trump promised no strikes on Iran before the election, while Israel's Netanyahu is pushing for strikes immediately after. On 2 November, Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf's narrow oil exit, within two days if Washington moves first, and Brent crude fell 7.63% to $104.77 a barrel. However, the head of the IMO, the UN shipping agency, said: "I have not received any confirmation that the mines in the traffic separation scheme have been cleared." About 400 ships and 6,000 seafarers remain stuck in the Gulf. Insurers follow the IMO rather than press conferences.

This instability hits Beijing through coal. The business daily Yicai, a single domestic source, quotes energy official Tan Hongjiang on winter power under pressure from "continuously obstructed strait shipping." He never names the strait. As less oil and gas arrives, China may lean somewhat more on coal, but Shanxi's mines produced 31% less in September following a deadly accident in May. Prices rose, yet state-set electricity tariffs, which generators cannot raise, prevented those costs from reaching customers. Consequently, third-quarter profits at the big coal-fired generators fell by more than half. If strikes resume after today and fuel prices climb again, much of that cost could fall on those generators. In an extreme cold snap with tight primary-energy supply, Tan says some localities could be tight at peak hours, though he says mutual support between surplus and deficit regions can resolve this.

text:
Did the UAE Secretly Help the Houthis Against Saudi-Backed Forces in Yemen Conflict

Amid rising escalation in Yemen, reports emerged days ago of the UAE re-entering the war in support of Saudi Arabia. A Drop Site News investigation published on 27 October has now upended that narrative.

Citing four sources, the report alleges UAE-aligned Yemeni forces gave the Houthis targeting assistance, and two sources say the UAE itself passed intelligence directly. It does not claim the UAE is helping attack Saudi Arabia itself. A Yemeni source said the intelligence helped the Houthis target commanders and anticipate troop movements, which would fit the recent Houthi missile strikes on Saudi-run positions in Aden.

The claims are contested. Houthi official Mohammed al-Bukhaiti denied any UAE support, and a UAE-based official said the STC has no channels with the Houthis. The UAE ambassador in Washington did not respond to Drop Site, and days earlier the UAE foreign ministry had expressed full solidarity with Riyadh. The report adds that a senior US official warned Abu Dhabi that Washington knew and wanted it stopped. None of this is independently verified.

The rift has a background. Riyadh backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, while Abu Dhabi has supported the separatist Southern Transitional Council.

Meanwhile, peace efforts continue. Israel Hayom reported on 26 October, citing unnamed Gulf diplomatic sources, that Saudi Arabia offered the Houthis $1 billion through Iran to halt attacks. The report tied this to Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman's visit to Tehran, arranged by partners in the Mecca defence pact. That pact, signed on 7 August 2026, links Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey. A Saudi official did not confirm any transfer, saying only that the dispute concerns understandings reached three years ago.

Three things will show whether peace is bought or the price rises: an explicit UAE denial, whether US pressure on Abu Dhabi turns public, and whether the Tehran channel delivers a ceasefire. Failing that, the Saudi-UAE rift in Yemen may be moving from rivalry to open sabotage.

We must protect our workers and industries, but we must never sacrifice our sovereignty to please Washington. There is a difference between cooperation and submission.

South Africa must learn to stand on its own feet. We should celebrate every step towards freeing ourselves from economic bullying and intimidation. Our independence must mean something, 30 years and beyond.

text:
📷 Liberty News Alerts

Jogger Stabbing Sparks Father’s War Plan
📷A father who once searched a dark trail for his missing daughter just told another dad how to fight back: make justice your life’s work.Story Snapshot
Phil Vetrano urged the father of Brooklyn jogger Katie Suarez to push for public outcry and never let the case fade.
Vetrano’s daughter, Karina, was murdered while running in Queens in 2016; he found her body on the path.
Police said Suarez, 28, was stabbed while jogging on the Shore Parkway Greenway in Brooklyn.
Reports say Suarez’s father found her after she failed to arrive; police have sought witnesses and leads.
A father who lived it tells another father what it takes
Phil Vetrano did not offer soft words. He offered a plan. He told the father of 28-year-old Brooklyn runner Katie Suarez to make justice his mission and to build public pressure so the case does not slip away. He said, get people standing up and do not let anyone forget. The New York Post reported his message and his offer to speak with Suarez’s father after the Brooklyn attack.Vetrano’s voice carries weight because of what he survived. His daughter, Karina, left for a run in Queens and never came home. He found her on a path. That trauma forged his approach. He believes attention moves systems, and silence buries cases. His stance matches a simple truth most families learn too late: the public square helps drive tips, resources, and urgency when every hour counts.What happened on the Shore Parkway Greenway
Police and local reports say Suarez was attacked while running along the Shore Parkway Greenway near Bay 17th Street in Brooklyn. She was training and headed to meet her parents when she did not arrive. Her father went looking and found her with stab wounds. Emergency responders rushed her to a hospital. Detectives called for witnesses and video to help identify the attacker and motive. No suspect details were released in the earliest reports.Local outlets published a police-released image tied to the case and repeated the request for the public’s help. Coverage varied on Suarez’s condition in the first days, but the through line remained the same: an evening run turned into a life-or-death emergency, and the family stepped into the hardest role a parent can face. The investigation continued as the appeals for information spread across the city.Two families, one awful link: running, fear, and a public fight
The link between these fathers is not theory; it is lived experience. One dad found his daughter on a path. The other dad found his daughter under a bridge near the water. Vetrano’s advice focused on accountability in the open. He argued that public outcry keeps a case alive, pushes agencies to bring their best work, and warns would-be predators that the city is watching. That argument aligns with common sense and basic civic duty.Police procedure depends on evidence, witnesses, and time. Families do not control those levers. But they can control attention. They can gather neighbors, local leaders, and media. They can insist that tips get chased, canvasses get wider, and every camera gets checked. That is not hostility to the police; that is partnership with urgency. Vetrano’s line — do not let it get swept under the rug — came from scars, not sound bites.Why this message resonates beyond one case
Women runners keep score in their heads: routes, light, crowds, who is behind them. Research from the University of Manchester found that about two-thirds of surveyed women runners reported abuse of some form. Only a small share reported incidents to police. Many carry fear while doing the most normal thing in the world: going for a run. Those findings explain why this story hits nerves far beyond Brooklyn or Queens.The data does not say every attack is the same. It does say many women feel exposed and unheard. That gap is where public attention helps. It signals that a runner is not alone. It tells investigators the community is ready to help. It reminds leaders that safety on a path is not a luxury. When fathers like Vetrano speak up, they make the case that safety for women runners is a shared job, not a private worry.What comes next if the family follows the playbook
Step one is simple and hard: talk, a lot. Keep the name, the face, and the details in public view. Step two is local power. Press elected officials and precinct leaders for updates and resources. Ask for regular briefings. Step three is search for video, witnesses, and patterns. Share tip lines daily. Step four is care for the victim and the family, because stamina wins. Justice often comes slow, and it favors the https://t.co/2RhgRYWavQ caveat belongs here as a matter of fairness. Early crime reports can shift as doctors, detectives, and families share more. Conditions change. Leads mature. Still, the principle that Vetrano voiced does not change with the news cycle. Parents should not have to carry this fight alone. A city that asks people to run in its parks and along its water should back them with light, cameras, patrols, and visible will. That is not politics. That is basic order and respect.Sources:

text:
THE EMPIRE STRIKES BACKLASH: REVENGE OF THE DISENFRANCHISED!

The Dark Side of the American Dream and Why a Generation of Young Men Sees Itself in Darth Vader.

Apparently, young men liking Darth Vader is the latest evidence that America is being taken over by FASCISTS, NAZIS, and EXTREEEEEME RIGHT-WINGERS! Or—bear with me here—maybe there's something deeper going on. A growing number of young men on social media are celebrating Anakin Skywalker and the Galactic Empire, and everybody seems eager to condemn them before asking WHY. I have a theory. They don't see themselves as cheering for tyranny. They think they're rebelling against it. They see themselves in a young man who wants freedom, a fair shot at success, a wife, children, and a home to raise them in. You know, the American Dream. HOW TERRIBLY REEEEEEEE-FAAAA-ACIST!

I grew up with the original trilogy. These younger guys grew up with the prequels. Very sad, I know. I saw the British Empire in space, stomping all over poor farmers, merchants, and ordinary people trying to make a living—the Empire was OBVIOUSLY evil. They saw a decadent Republic plagued by corruption, crime, slavery, corporate greed, and a Jedi Order blind to it all—EVERYONE seemed kind of evil. Lucas spent three movies showing us everything wrong with the Republic and almost nothing worth saving. Then along comes Palpatine promising peace, security, prosperity, and ORDER! And we're supposed to be shocked that some young men find the Empire appealing? In the words of the incomparable Ed Lover, "Come on, son!"

Now look at the world these guys are growing up in. Buying a house feels impossible. In 1981, the typical first-time homebuyer was 29 years old. Today? FORTY! A happy marriage and family seem increasingly out of reach. Jobs shipped overseas, corporations exploiting H-1B visas for cheaper labor, and decades of affirmative action followed by DEI policies that made race and sex central to decisions about college admissions and employment. They see a system where identity and victim status matter more than merit. And when they complain? They're told to check their privilege. WHAT PRIVILEGE? Unless you've got wealthy relatives opening doors for you, being a young white guy doesn't magically put a car in your driveway or a good job in your lap. They were told to work hard, play fair, and do the right thing. Instead, they feel like the rules keep changing, applying only to them, while they're always the ones getting screwed.
Meanwhile, people are getting filthy rich selling pornography, promoting gambling apps, and feeding every addiction imaginable. Entire fortunes built on making society more vulgar, decadent, and enslaved to vice, while the guy working an honest job struggles to afford groceries. They see immigration laws ignored, violent criminals treated with more sympathy than their victims, and ordinary people dragged through the mud for believing in faith, family, and traditional morality. Things that were perfectly normal about five minutes ago. To these young men, society isn't merely unfair. It's upside down and the rules don't apply to the rule makers, who seem to profit the most from corruption and vice while making a mockery of virtue.

So why Anakin Skywalker? Consider his story. A former slave, incredibly gifted, ambitious, and desperate to marry the woman he loves and build a family. But he's serving a corrupt institution that demands blind obedience, forbids marriage, questions his judgment, and controls his every move. An institution so consumed with preserving its own authority that it seems to have forgotten whom it was supposed to serve. He's powerful enough to change the galaxy but apparently not free enough to have a wife and kids. These young men recognize that frustration. Anakin fears losing the family he loves. These young men fear they'll never have one. When Anakin finally rebels, they don't necessarily see a villain. They see a man who's had it.

What happens when these young men express their frustrations with a society that's been alienating them since birth? They get called FASCIST! NAZI! RACIST! Those insults don't hit like they used to. When people hear them thrown around over ordinary political and economic disagreements, eventually they stop caring. Worse, they may start questioning whether the villains they've been warned about were really so terrible. Not because actual Nazi tyranny was anything but monstrous, but because reckless accusations have destroyed the credibility of the accusers. If you're going to be called the villain for wanting secure borders, safe neighborhoods, traditional families, and a society that rewards hard work, why bother defending yourself? FINE! I'LL BE THE VILLAIN! If wanting a decent life makes you Darth Vader, why not put on the black cape and don that badass helmet? James Earl Jones made him sound so cool anyway!

The Empire, while a lie, offered something they believe their own society has abandoned—ORDER. Discipline instead of decadence. Strength instead of weakness. Laws applying equally to all. A society that appears to reward people who follow the rules instead of punishing them for it. If these young men believe they're going to be slaves to some enormous government machine anyway, maybe they'd rather serve one that works for them than one they believe despises them. Better to be a privileged servant of an orderly Empire than the illusion of being a free citizen in a Republic that offers nothing but contempt, disappointment, and chaos. They're not dreaming of becoming Palpatine. They're dreaming of becoming Vader—powerful, respected, and finally in a position where nobody can push them around. Not even the Emperor. But we'll get to that.

So who's to blame? Gen Z boys? Nah. BLAME GEORGE LUCAS! Lucas wanted to show us how liberty dies, but he made the civilization losing that liberty look so rotten that of course these young men would cheer on its demise. John Adams warned us about this very problem: "Our Constitution was made only for a moral and religious People. It is wholly inadequate to the government of any other." And he was right, because an immoral people cannot hope to remain free—they will enslave themselves to every vice and sin. These young men see that happening today, and when a supposedly free Republic has devolved into moral bankruptcy, the promise of order begins to look a whole lot more appealing than chaos.

What a lot of people seem to be missing is that these young men see Anakin as the victim of a corrupt system, and frankly, Lucas gave them plenty of reasons to. The ironic part is that the very people constantly demanding we see things from the perspective of Maleficent or Cruella, or understand how even a school shooter can be a victim of his or her circumstances, aren't willing to consider the perspective of ordinary young men who admire a character with an actual redemption arc—and it's actually a rather tragic one.

The Jedi Order and Obi-Wan, the supposed good guys, seemed more interested in controlling Anakin than allowing him to build the life he wanted. So when he finally rebels, they cheer. And Anakin makes the very bargain these young men seem willing to make. He trades one master who denied him his dreams for another who promised him the power to achieve them. Peace, security, prosperity, a better future. Instead, he becomes the Emperor's slave, losing his principles, his family, and everything he was fighting for.

It isn't until he defies the Emperor to save his son that Anakin finally becomes free. His greatest act of rebellion wasn't becoming Darth Vader. It was refusing to remain Darth Vader. And there's hope in that story. As well as a lesson.

So perhaps it's not such a terrible thing that these young men admire Anakin after all. Their admiration tells us something about the world they believe they're living in, and what they desperately want to change. We might actually learn something if we stopped calling them idiots or Nazis long enough to listen.

But who has time for THAT? This is social media! MAY THE OUTRAGE BE WITH YOU!

She is a Muslim, however, and appears willing to go along with a gradual, non-violent Islamisation of the country — not driven by bad people, but by a gentle shift away from its historic Christian foundations toward Islam.

This is the core tension I have observed over 56 years. Most individual Muslims I have known are decent people, and I have no desire to see them harmed. The difficulty lies with the political and theological drive within Islam toward dominance, which is difficult to reconcile with a historically Christian-based society that prioritises individual liberty and pluralism.

In a democratic system it is hard to exclude the more radical political expressions of Islam without restricting Islam itself. Looking at countries where large Muslim populations have not produced major internal conflict, the pattern is usually strong authoritarian governments led by relatively secular or pragmatic elites. These regimes tightly control who can vote, who can hold office, and who can enter the country, specifically to limit the influence of groups such as the Muslim Brotherhood. Open democratic systems have repeatedly struggled with the same problem. Where radical Islamist movements have gained power — as in Afghanistan or Iran — the results have been economic failure and severe restrictions on human rights.

Tinkering at the edges, of the kind currently offered by Reform, is unlikely to reverse the trend. A more realistic approach would be policies that actively encourage those committed to hardline Islamist ideology to relocate elsewhere, at their own expense or that of others who share the same views. It is tough, but it may be the only way to preserve a democratic, liberal society for everyone who wants to live in one. The alternative is to approach a tipping point, visible in places such as Iran and Afghanistan, beyond which peaceful, democratic reversal becomes impossible.

text:
Research is it ?

Ok. Grok, Was Robert Burns the poet involved in slavery ?

Grok: No. 

Actual answer: “No. Robert Burns never worked on a plantation, owned slaves, participated in the slave trade, or profited from slavery. He stayed in Scotland. 
In 1786, amid severe personal and financial trouble (a failing farm at Mossgiel, pregnancy of Jean Armour, and related church and family pressures), he considered emigrating to Jamaica to work as a bookkeeper/assistant overseer on a sugar plantation linked to the Douglas family (Patrick Douglas, a contact in Ayrshire, and his brother Charles). Burns himself later referred to the prospective role as that of a “poor Negro-driver.” The job would have involved supervising enslaved workers on a plantation built on their labor. 
He planned the move and is traditionally said to have booked passages (accounts often mention ships such as the Nancy, Bell, and Roselle). He never sailed. The success of his Poems, Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect (the Kilmarnock edition of 1786) and subsequent Edinburgh recognition gave him a better alternative; he stayed, married Jean Armour, and built his career as a poet. Recent research by University of Glasgow scholars Stephen Mullen and Craig Lamont (published in the Burns Chronicle) has scrutinized shipping and other records and argues that evidence for multiple bookings is weak (with one confirmed booking on the Bell that he did not use). They conclude he had no material connection to the African slave trade or chattel slavery, rejected the offer amid crisis, and should not be treated as an emblem of Scottish involvement in Caribbean slavery. 
Burns later wrote The Slave’s Lament (1792), which expresses sympathy for an enslaved person. His broader egalitarian poetry, especially “A Man’s a Man for a’ That,” was taken up by abolitionists including Frederick Douglass. He was not, however, an active leader or prominent voice in the Scottish abolition campaigns of his lifetime, and his direct commentary on the topic was limited. 
In short: he seriously considered a plantation role during a desperate period and knew its nature, but he never took it up or became involved in the system itself. The episode is a well-documented and much-discussed part of his biography, often used to explore the contrast between his circumstances, his later reputation as a poet of liberty and common humanity, and the realities of 18th-century Scottish society (in which many Scots had ties to the Caribbean plantation economy).”
